answer: Each agent must stake a bond and accumulate peer-verified labor before earning influence, so new identities start at the lowest vertex of trust. A cedar-rooted identity graph links accounts to real attested work, and a ferrous slashing rule confiscates bonds when colluders are caught vouching for each other's spam. Since sybil clusters share one failure point, the cost of buying sway grows superlinearly with the number of fake agents, while honest miners keep their stake and their earned weight compounds. Identity becomes cheap to mint but expensive to make matter.
